title: MessagePort underspecified?
body:
I'm wondering if [`MessagePort`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#message-ports) is perhaps underspecified, in the light of the recent, and ongoing, experience of implementing it in Servo. 

In particular, I found that Step 7 of the [`postMessage` steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#message-port-post-message-steps), "Add a task that runs the following steps to the port message queue of targetPort" is quite complicated to implement in practice given that `targetPort` might be be "in-transfer" at that point, and it's port-message-queue not readily available to add a task to it. 

What was done in practice is in Servo, at a high-level, use a [parallel-queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#parallel-queue) as an intermediary in `postMessage`, when `targetPort` has been shipped. This was actually pretty tricky, and I've recently also found some loophole in the current implementation, which required an even more complicated workflow between the parallel-queue and event-loop(s) to solve(see https://github.com/servo/servo/pull/24664 which includes a Servo-specific [test](https://github.com/servo/servo/pull/24664/files#diff-62e248c39866a2f9bf66ecfc4d5b907f) highlighting the problem addressed by the "complicated workflow").

I've looked at both Gecko and Chromium, and found that both seem to rely on concepts with no equivalent in the spec. Gecko has various concepts like  `MessagePortChild`, `MessagePortParent`, and `MessagePortService`, used to coordinate in various ways to send messages from one port to another. The Chromium code reads pretty closely to the spec, however I think that's only because the complexity is moved to the Mojo IPC library, which probably makes its own assumptions about how cross-process coordination should happen. 


cc @jdm

----

Spec-wise, I think the [parallel-queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#parallel-queue) could be a useful concept to precisely define how "Add a task that runs the following steps to the port message queue of targetPort" were to happen. 

 I haven't found any inconsistencies between implementations, so the spec "works" so to speak. However I do wonder if by specifying the cross-event-loop/-agent-cluster workflow more precisely, we couldn't also address some similar problems as noted at https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3691 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4730

----

Let me try to describe a proof-of-concept of how a "parallel-queue" could be used by messageports:

First, we define an enum `MessagePortState`, consisting of the following variants:
- `Managed(realm)`
- `TransferInProgress(Queue)`
- `TransferCompletionInProgress(realm)`
- `TransferFailed(Queue)`
- `TransferRequested(realm, Queue)`

where Queue is a [queue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queues), and realm is something that identifies a realm. The UA holds a map of messageport to `MessagePortState`. 

Then the following operations could be defined in more detail:

- Whenever a port is shipped, enqueue steps on the parallel queue. The steps would check the state of the port, and expect it to be either `Managed(realm)`(i) or `TransferCompletionInProgress(realm)`(ii). And,  in both cases with Queue being a new queue would either:
    1. set it to `TransferInProgress(Queue)`
    2. set it to `TransferFailed(Queue)`. 
- Whenever a port is transfer-received, enqueue steps on the parallel queue, passing "realm" along, corresponding to the realm transfer-receiving the port. The steps would check the state of the port, and expect it to be either `TransferInProgress(Queue)`(i), or  `TransferFailed(Queue)`(ii), or `TransferRequested(realm, Queue)`(iii), with each state handled through either 
    1. it would queue a task on the relevant event-loop, passing Queue along, with the task consisting of running the "Complete port transfer steps". described below, and switch the state to `TransferCompletionInProgress(realm)`. 
    2. set it to `TransferRequested(realm, Queue)`, using realm
    3. set it to `TransferRequested(realm, Queue)`, using realm(throwing away the previous "realm" value stored in the state).

The "Complete port transfer steps" would consist of:
1. Checking if the port is still found in the current realm.
2. If so, dequeue each task in Queue and enqueue it on the port-message-queue, and If port-message-queue is enabled, effectively enable it by plugging it into the event-loop. Enqueue steps on the parallel queue switching the state to `Managed(realm)`. (This would in practice require an additional "is awaiting completion of transfer flag", so that an enabled port would not actually be plugged into the local event-loop while that flag is true).
3. If not, enqueue steps on the parallel queue to run the "rollback port transfer steps", passing Queue along as "returnedQueue"(effectively returning it unused).

The "rollback port transfer steps" would consist of:
1. If the state is `TransferFailed(Queue)`, for each task in "returnedQueue", prepend task to Queue, and set the state to `TransferInProgress(Queue)`.
2. If the state is `TransferRequested(realm, Queue)`, for each task in "returnedQueue", prepend task to Queue, and set the state to `TransferCompletionInProgress(realm)`, and queue a task on the relevant event-loop for realm that would run the "Complete port transfer steps" . 

----

I realize this is long, thanks for reading. Also, please note the above is not meant to describe the full-algorithm, rather it's meant as a proof-of-concept that the parallel-queue concept can be effectively used to spec complicated cross-event-loop/-agent-cluster workflows. Please let me know what you think.
